findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Label the `add-json` one-liner as POSIX-shell syntax and give a Windows alternative, e.g. editing the `mcpServers` entry in `~/.claude.json` directly with the same `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}` header.
evidence: "replace the ... command with `claude mcp add-json -s user rebar '<json>'` ... where the single-quoted JSON carries the literal `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`"
Platform fact: cmd.exe has no single-quote quoting; Windows PowerShell 5.1 mangles embedded double quotes in native-command arguments.
findings.finding:
The documented Claude Code user-level fallback relies on POSIX shell single-quoting (`claude mcp add-json -s user rebar '<json>'`). On Windows this fails:
- `cmd.exe` does not treat single quotes as quoting, so the JSON is split into several arguments.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 strips the embedded double quotes when passing arguments to a native executable.

Either way `claude mcp add-json` receives invalid JSON. A Windows user following the doc gets an error and may fall back to the `--header` form the doc warns against.
findings.location: Approach — Claude Code bullet: "`claude mcp add-json -s user rebar '<json>'` ... where the single-quoted JSON carries the literal `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}` placeholder"
scenarios: Windows/cmd.exe developer workstation: `claude mcp add-json` reports a JSON parse error and no server is added.
Windows PowerShell 5.1: the argument arrives as `{type:http,...}` without quotes, giving invalid JSON and the setup fails.
